DILAWAR / MOLECULAR GEOMETRY

A closer look at a molecular path.

Butane, trans to gauche. Rotate the molecule, follow its torsion, and inspect every interpolated geometry.

Drag to rotate · scroll or pinch to zoom
Highlighted: C1–C2–C3–C4

Geometry along the path

Geodesic

Choose a coordinate to highlight its atoms. Click a graph to select an image. Dihedrals are unwrapped along each continuous, defined segment.

Track your own coordinate

Use the atom numbers shown in the molecular view. Distances can include any pair, including nonbonded contacts.

Atom numbers are 1-based; carbon atoms are 1–4 and hydrogen atoms are 5–14.

Take the data with you

Export the full sequence or the currently selected geometry. CSV includes selected and automatically enumerated coordinates for both paths.

What this example shows

Idealized tetrahedral butane endpoints, with a fixed atom mapping and reference bond graph. All 101 requested images enter geodesic optimization; none are added just for playback.

This is a geometric interpolation, without a physical time axis or an energy-minimized reaction path. Optimizer convergence is not certified. The Cartesian baseline connects the same aligned endpoint frames.
